title_en: Dalian Zhitai Seed Industry Co., Ltd. v. Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs Plant New Variety Review Committee et al. — administrative dispute over invalidation of plant new variety rights
ruling_gist_en: The existence of a sales act is an important fact in determining whether an applied variety possesses novelty. A sale that causes the loss of novelty of a variety for which the protection of a new plant variety right is applied refers to an act by which an actor, for the purpose of trading, delivers the reproductive material of the variety to another person for disposal, thereby relinquishing its own right of disposal over such reproductive material. Where a breeder delivers the reproductive material of the applied variety to another person for the purpose of commissioning the production of seeds, and at the same time agrees that the produced variety reproductive material shall be returned to the breeder, since the breeder substantially retains the right of disposal over the variety reproductive material, unless otherwise provided by law, the applied variety will not lose its novelty.
keywords_en: Administrative; Administrative dispute over invalidation of new plant variety rights; Second instance; Supreme People's Court; Beijing; Liaoning Province; Legal person; Natural person; Regulations on the Protection of New Plant Varieties; Determination of sales act; Loss of variety novelty; Whether commissioned seed production constitutes a sale; Affirm original judgment; Invalidation of new plant variety rights; Corn variety; Commissioned seed production; Variety approval; Clarify determination standards for sales act; Unify rules for novelty determination; Intellectual property
full_text_en:
Dalian Zhitai Seed Industry Co., Ltd. v. Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs Plant Variety Protection Review Board, et al. — administrative dispute over invalidation of new plant variety rights

[Ruling Summary]

The existence of sales activities is an important fact in determining whether an applied variety possesses novelty. The sale that causes the loss of novelty of a variety for which protection as a new plant variety is sought refers to the act by which a person, for the purpose of trading, delivers the propagating material of the variety to another person for disposal, thereby relinquishing his own right to dispose of such propagating material. Where a breeder delivers the applied variety's propagating material to another person for the purpose of commissioning the production of seeds, and simultaneously agrees that the produced variety's propagating material shall be returned to the breeder, the breeder essentially retains the right to dispose of such propagating material, and unless otherwise provided by law, this will not cause the applied variety to lose its novelty.

Supreme People's Court Administrative Judgment

(2022) Zui Gao Fa Zhi Zhong Zhong No. 809

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): Dalian Zhitai Seed Industry Co., Ltd. Domicile: Jinchang Village, Fengrong Subdistrict Office, Pulandian District, Dalian City, Liaoning Province.

Legal Representative: Gong Xianqi, General Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Xiao Chunyang, Lawyer of Liaoning Boxin Law Firm.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs Plant Variety Protection Review Board. Domicile: No. 11, Nongzhanguan Nanli, Chaoyang District, Beijing.

Responsible Person: Zhang Xingwang, Director of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Tao Weiguo, Male, Director of Variety Management Division, Seed Industry Management Department, Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs.

Agent ad litem: Chen Meng, Lawyer of Beijing Tianchi Juntai Law Firm.

Third Party at First Instance: Yi Tailong, Male, born on January 28, 1956, Han nationality, domiciled in Donggang Town, Wafangdian City, Liaoning Province.

Agent ad litem: Liang Shunwei, Lawyer of Beijing Kaiyue Law Firm.

In the administrative dispute over invalidation of new plant variety rights between the Appellant Dalian Zhitai Seed Industry Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zhitai Company) and the Appellee Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs Plant Variety Protection Review Board (hereinafter referred to as the Plant Variety Protection Review Board) and the Third Party at First Instance Yi Tailong, the case involves a corn new plant variety named "Qiangshuo 68" (hereinafter referred to as the variety in question) with the variety rights holder being Yi Tailong. In response to the request for invalidation of the variety rights in question filed by Zhitai Company, the Plant Variety Protection Review Board issued Decision No. 2020-25 on Review of Invalidity of Variety Rights (hereinafter referred to as the Decision under Review), maintaining the validity of the variety rights in question. Dissatisfied, Zhitai Company filed a lawsuit with the Beijing Intellectual Property Court (hereinafter referred to as the court of first instance). The court of first instance issued Administrative Judgment (2021) Jing 73 Xing Chu No. 3144 on August 17, 2022, dismissing Zhitai Company's claims. Dissatisfied, Zhitai Company appealed to this Court. After filing the appeal on November 23, 2022, this Court formed a collegial panel according to law and held a public hearing on February 28, 2023. The Appellant Zhitai Company's agent ad litem Xiao Chunyang, the Appellee Plant Variety Protection Review Board's agents ad litem Tao Weiguo and Chen Meng, and the Third Party at First Instance Yi Tailong's agent ad litem Liang Shunwei appeared in court. The case has now been concluded.

The basic facts of this case are as follows: The variety in question is a corn new plant variety named "Qiangshuo 68" with variety rights number CNA20090802.7, the variety rights holder is Yi Tailong, the application date is December 9, 2009, and the authorization date is March 1, 2014.

On January 24, 2019, Zhitai Company requested the Plant Variety Protection Review Board to declare the variety rights of "Qiangshuo 68" invalid on the ground that the variety rights in question lacked novelty. Zhitai Company submitted the following 10 pieces of evidence:

1. Certificate of New Plant Variety Rights for "Qiangshuo 68".

2. Letter of Certification issued by Zhangye Dunhuang Seed Industry Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zhangye Dunhuang Company) to the Shenyang Intermediate People's Court of Liaoning Province on October 20, 2015. It states: "Our company accepted the entrustment of Yi Tailong to cultivate Qiangshuo 68 corn seeds for him from 2008 to the present. Based on our consistent production and operation practices, after calculation, our company delivered Qiangshuo 68 corn seeds to Yi Tailong at a price of RMB 6.3 per kilogram."

3. Letter of Reply from Gansu Provincial Seed Administration Bureau to Dalian Pulandian Agricultural Administrative Law Enforcement Brigade dated March 13, 2018, concerning "Licensing Qualifications for the Variety 'Qiangshuo 68' of Gansu Dunhuang Seed Industry Co., Ltd." It states: "Upon inquiry, the original seed production license held by Gansu Dunhuang Seed Industry Co., Ltd. was (Gan) Nong Zhong Sheng Xu Zi (2006) No. 0026, with the license issuance date of October 27, 2006, and validity period until October 27, 2009. During the validity period of the license, on June 24, 2008, the enterprise amended and added the corn variety 'Qiangshuo 68'."

4. Request from Dalian Seed Management Station of Liaoning Province to Dalian Rural Economic Committee of Liaoning Province dated January 10, 2008, regarding "Regulations on Sales Management of Hybrid Corn and Rice Varieties for 2008" (Da Zhong Guan Zi [2008] No. 2).

5. Notice issued by Dalian Rural Economic Committee of Liaoning Province on January 15, 2008, on "Strengthening Sales Management of Hybrid Corn and Rice Varieties" (Da Nong Fa [2008] No. 7).

6. Letter of Reply from Dalian Seed Management Station of Liaoning Province to Zhitai Company dated March 1, 2017, titled "Reply to Request Letter of Dalian Zhitai Seed Industry Co., Ltd."

7. Notice issued by the Seed Administration Bureau of the former Ministry of Agriculture on May 11, 2015, on "Revocation of Standard Samples of the Certified Corn Variety 'Zhitai No. 1'" (Nong Zhong Pin Han [2015] No. 20).

8. Variety Certification Certificate for "Qiangshuo 68" issued by the Liaoning Provincial Crop Variety Approval Committee on February 21, 2008. Certificate No.: 2007-1-35; Crop: Corn; Approval No.: Liao Shen Yu [2007] No. 351; Approved Name: Qiangshuo 68; Original Name or Code: Haosheng No. 6; Breeding Unit (Individual): Yi Tailong.

9. Excerpts from the "Administrative Measures for Seed Production and Operation Licenses for Crops" (Order No. 48 of the former Ministry of Agriculture, February 26, 2001).

10. "Implementing Rules of the Regulations of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of New Plant Varieties (Agricultural Part)" (Revised in 2007) (hereinafter referred to as the Implementing Rules of the Regulations).

On January 28, 2019, after formal examination, the Plant Variety Protection Review Board issued a Notice of Acceptance to Zhitai Company.

On February 27, 2019, the Plant Variety Protection Review Board issued a Notice of Supplementary Materials to Zhitai Company, requiring Zhitai Company to provide more convincing evidence and supporting grounds, within one month from the date of receipt of the notice, focusing on the facts of the production agreement in the review request. On March 5, 2019, Zhitai Company submitted a Statement of Opinion to the Plant Variety Protection Review Board, arguing that the probative force of the existing evidence was sufficient to prove that "Qiangshuo 68" lacked novelty.

On March 27, 2019, Yi Tailong submitted to the Plant Variety Protection Review Board an "Explanation of Circumstances Concerning the 'Novelty' of Variety 'Qiangshuo 68'", presenting the following four points of defense: (1) "Qiangshuo 68" obtained variety certification on February 21, 2008. In that year, there were no large quantities of propagating material available for commercial production, so Yi Tailong asked Zhangye Dunhuang Company to help arrange small-scale trial production of "Qiangshuo 68" seeds. The parent seeds were provided free of charge, and the two parties did not sign a seed production agreement. (2) Under normal circumstances, small-scale trial production of seeds generally does not require a seed production license. However, Gansu Dunhuang Seed Industry Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Gansu Dunhuang Company), in order to undertake seed production business in 2009, submitted materials for obtaining a seed production license for "Qiangshuo 68" to the local agricultural department one year in advance. Gansu Dunhuang Company amended and added the corn variety "Qiangshuo 68" on June 24, 2008, within the validity period of its seed production license, which cannot prove that Yi Tailong and Gansu Dunhuang Company had signed a seed production agreement for "Qiangshuo 68" before that date. (3) Yi Tailong began large-scale production of "Qiangshuo 68" seeds in 2009, and applied for new plant variety protection on December 9, 2009. The variety in question has not lost its novelty. (4) Yi Tailong had previously sued Zhitai Company for infringement of his "Qiangshuo 68" variety rights. The case went through first instance, second instance, and application for retrial, i.e., Civil Judgment (2015) Shen Zhong Min Chu Zi No. 00240 rendered by the Shenyang Intermediate People's Court of Liaoning Province (hereinafter referred to as the No. 240 Judgment), Civil Judgment (2016) Liao Min Zhong No. 460 rendered by the Liaoning High People's Court, and Civil Ruling (2017) Zui Gao Fa Min Shen No. 2362 rendered by the Supreme People's Court (hereinafter referred to as the No. 2362 Ruling). All courts supported Yi Tailong's claims. In addition, in June 2016, Zhitai Company had already filed a request for invalidation on the ground that "Qiangshuo 68" lacked novelty, and the Plant Variety Protection Review Board rejected that invalidation request.

Together with the "Explanation of Circumstances Concerning the 'Novelty' of Variety 'Qiangshuo 68'", Yi Tailong submitted three counter-evidence items to the Plant Variety Protection Review Board as follows:

Counter-Evidence 1: "Explanation of the Production of 'Qiangshuo 68' Hybrid Corn Seeds" issued by Zhangye Dunhuang Company on February 21, 2019. It records the specific matters of the cooperation between Zhangye Dunhuang Company and Yi Tailong in 2009 for the production of "Qiangshuo 68" corn seeds: (1) In 2008, Zhangye Dunhuang Company assisted Yi Tailong in starting trial production of two corn varieties, mainly to debug the corn seed production flowering schedule plan and observe the adaptability of the varieties. However, during the trial production process, the flowering schedule was not properly adjusted, resulting in a mismatch in flowering periods and failed seed production. (2) Through the trial production observation in 2008, it was determined that "Qiangshuo 68" could be produced in the region, and a seed production plan was explored based on the trial. (3) To meet the production and sales needs for the following year, materials for the licensing qualification of the corn variety "Qiangshuo 68" were submitted to the Gansu Provincial Seed Management Station in advance in June 2008, and the seed production license was obtained on June 24, 2008. (4) Formal cooperation in the production of commissioned seeds began in 2009.

Counter-Evidence 2: The No. 2362 Ruling. It states: Regarding Zhitai Company's asserted ground for retrial that the "Qiangshuo 68" variety rights should be invalidated, this disputed issue is a matter to be resolved in the invalidation procedure of variety rights, not a key issue to be examined in the civil infringement procedure of that case. Therefore, Zhitai Company's above ground for retrial is not supported.

Counter-Evidence 3: The Review Decision on Invalidity of Variety Rights concerning "Qiangshuo 68" (Decision No. 2017-2) issued by the Plant Variety Protection Review Board on May 16, 2017. The requester in that invalidation proceeding was Zhitai Company, and the grounds for invalidation were that "Qiangshuo 68" and "Zhitai No. 1" were the same variety, lacking distinctness and novelty. The evidence submitted by Zhitai Company included: the No. 240 Judgment; Inspection Report (Nong) Zhong Zhong Jian Zi (2011) No. 001 issued by the Beijing Corn Seed Testing Center; and the warehouse outbound ledger and delivery vouchers for "Zhitai No. 1". The Plant Variety Protection Review Board ultimately determined that the evidence submitted by Zhitai Company could not prove that "Qiangshuo 68" did not meet the requirements of distinctness and novelty for new plant varieties, and thus rejected Zhitai Company's invalidation request.

On August 1, 2019, the Plant Variety Protection Review Board exchanged Yi Tailong's "Explanation of Circumstances Concerning the 'Novelty' of Variety 'Qiangshuo 68'" with Zhitai Company and issued a Notice of Statement of Opinion, requiring Zhitai Company to submit a statement of opinion in response to Yi Tailong's above explanation within three months from the date of receipt of the notice.

On September 17, 2019, Zhitai Company submitted a Statement of Opinion to the Plant Variety Protection Review Board, arguing that the Letter of Certification issued by Zhangye Dunhuang Company to the Shenyang Intermediate People's Court of Liaoning Province fully proved that Zhangye Dunhuang Company accepted Yi Tailong's entrustment to produce "Qiangshuo 68" corn seeds for him in 2008 and delivered the seeds to Yi Tailong that year. Moreover, Gansu Dunhuang Company could only obtain the production license for "Qiangshuo 68" by submitting the production agreement entrusted by the variety rights holder. The variety "Qiangshuo 68" had been sold for more than one year before the application date for its variety rights, thus losing its novelty.

On June 17, 2020, the Secretariat of the Plant Variety Protection Review Board issued a letter to the Gansu Provincial Seed Administration Bureau titled "Letter Requesting Assistance in Investigating the Production License Archives of 'Qiangshuo 68'", requesting the bureau to investigate and verify the "Letter of Reply on Licensing Qualifications for the Variety 'Qiangshuo 68' of Gansu Dunhuang Seed Industry Co., Ltd." and the production license archives and actual production situation of "Qiangshuo 68". On July 20, 2020, the Gansu Provincial Seed General Station issued a letter titled "Letter on the Seed Production Licensing Situation of 'Qiangshuo 68'" in response to the above letter. The specific reply was: (1) Production licensing situation of Gansu Dunhuang Company for "Qiangshuo 68". Upon inquiry, in June 2008, Gansu Dunhuang Company submitted an application for a production license for "Qiangshuo 68". After review by the Linze County Agriculture and Rural Affairs Bureau, acceptance by the Provincial Government Hall of the Agriculture and Animal Husbandry Department Window of Gansu Province, and approval by the Gansu Provincial Agriculture and Animal Husbandry Department, the enterprise's major crop seed production license was approved on June 24, 2008, to amend and add the production license for the variety "Qiangshuo 68". (2) Regarding the reply to the Dalian Pulandian Agricultural Administrative Law Enforcement Brigade. The Dalian Pulandian Agricultural Administrative Law Enforcement Brigade sent a letter on March 5, 2018, inquiring about the production licensing situation of "Qiangshuo 68" of Gansu Dunhuang Company. After verifying the relevant licensing information, on March 13, 2018, a "Letter of Reply on Licensing Qualifications for the Variety 'Qiangshuo 68' of Gansu Dunhuang Seed Industry Co., Ltd." was sent to the Dalian Pulandian Agricultural Administrative Law Enforcement Brigade.

On December 19, 2020, the Plant Variety Protection Review Board issued the Decision under Review, rejecting Zhitai Company's invalidation request and maintaining the validity of the "Qiangshuo 68" variety rights.

Dissatisfied, Zhitai Company filed a lawsuit with the court of first instance on February 20, 2021, requesting: a judgment to revoke the Decision under Review and order the Plant Variety Protection Review Board to make a new decision. The facts and reasons were: (1) "Qiangshuo 68" had already lost its "novelty" on June 24, 2008, and could not be authorized. Gansu Dunhuang Company held seed production license (Gan) Nong Zhong Sheng Xu Zi (2006) No. 0026, and on June 24, 2008, it added the production license for the corn variety "Qiangshuo 68". From 2008 to 2015, Zhangye Dunhuang Company accepted Yi Tailong's entrustment to cultivate "Qiangshuo 68" corn seeds for him, and sold "Qiangshuo 68" corn seeds to Yi Tailong at a price of RMB 6.3 per kilogram based on production and operation practices. The prerequisite for the Gansu Provincial Seed Administration Bureau to add a seed production license was the signing of a production agreement between the two parties. The addition of the production license and the entrustment for production sufficiently proved that the two parties had signed an entrustment production agreement before June 24, 2008. According to Article 14 of the Regulations of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of New Plant Varieties (Promulgated in 1997) (hereinafter referred to as the Regulations on the Protection of New Plant Varieties) and the relevant provisions of the Implementing Rules of the Regulations, "Qiangshuo 68" had been sold within China with the breeder's permission on June 24, 2008, and by the application date of December 9, 2009, the propagating material of the variety had been sold for one year and five months, exceeding one year. Thus, "Qiangshuo 68" lost its "novelty" and could not obtain variety rights.

The Plant Variety Protection Review Board argued in its defense at first instance: (1) The Plant Variety Protection Review Board has the statutory authority to accept and hear invalidation request review cases. The Decision under Review complies with legal and regulatory procedural requirements. (2) The evidence submitted by Zhitai Company cannot prove that Yi Tailong engaged in the sale of "Qiangshuo 68" or signed a related production agreement, and cannot prove that "Qiangshuo 68" lost its novelty. (3) According to the investigation conducted by the Plant Variety Protection Review Board, no production agreement or sales evidence for "Qiangshuo 68" was found. Zhitai Company's claims lack factual basis. The Decision under Review has clear factual findings and correct application of laws and regulations. Zhitai Company's grounds for the lawsuit are untenable, and the court is requested to dismiss its claims.

Yi Tailong stated at first instance: The facts on which Zhitai Company filed this lawsuit do not comply with the relevant legal provisions. "Qiangshuo 68" has not lost its novelty. Zhitai Company's claims should be dismissed.

The court of first instance essentially confirmed the above facts after trial.

The court of first instance additionally found: Zhitai Company submitted five pieces of evidence to the court of first instance, among which Evidence 4 was not submitted in the new plant variety invalidation procedure. Evidence 4 was the No. 240 Judgment. The judgment recorded the plaintiff as Yi Tailong and the defendant as Zhitai Company, with the cause of action as dispute over infringement of new plant variety rights. The variety for which Yi Tailong asserted rights was "Qiangshuo 68", and the allegedly infringing propagating material was "Zhitai No. 1" corn seeds. The judgment found that Zhitai Company, without the permission of the variety rights holder Yi Tailong, produced and sold "Qiangshuo 68" corn seeds under the name "Zhitai No. 1" for commercial purposes, thereby infringing upon Yi Tailong's new plant variety rights in "Qiangshuo 68". Zhitai Company shall bear civil liability for cessation of infringement and compensation for losses. Pages 11-12 of the judgment, regarding the focal issue of determining the amount of compensation, stated: "In this case, Yi Tailong, when filing the lawsuit, had already claimed to determine the amount of compensation based on the profits obtained by the infringer from the infringement. Therefore, this court determines the amount of compensation in this case based on Zhitai Company's profits from the infringement. The specific amount, because Zhitai Company refused to submit account books and materials concerning the production and sale of the infringing seeds to this court, is determined based on the existing evidence. According to the '2013-2014 Annual Survey Form for Sales and Inventory of Major Crop Seeds' submitted by Yi Tailong from the Dalian Seed Management Station, this court discretionarily determines that the average unit price at which Zhitai Company sold the infringing seeds at that time was RMB 10 per kilogram, the average monthly sales volume was 50,000 kilograms, and the sales amount was RMB 500,000. Therefore, the sales volume for the ten months from March 1, 2014, to the end of 2014 was approximately 500,000 kilograms, and the total sales amount was approximately RMB 5 million. Regarding the profit margin of Zhitai Company’s infringing seeds, because Zhitai Company refused to submit its account books on production and sales costs, and with reference to the unit cost certificate for producing 'Qiangshuo 68' corn seeds issued by other seed production enterprises submitted by Yi Tailong, it can be determined that the profit per kilogram was RMB 3.7. Therefore, the profit gained by Zhitai Company from selling 500,000 kilograms of infringing seeds is discretionarily determined to be RMB 1.85 million."

Upon the application of Zhitai Company, the court of first instance issued a "Letter of Entrusted Investigation" to the Gansu Provincial Seed Station on December 20, 2021, entrusting Zhitai Company's agent, Attorney Zheng Hua, to inquire and obtain all archives related to the production permit for the "Qiangshuo 68" corn variety formed or designated as before December 9, 2009 (inclusive). The Gansu Provincial Seed Station issued a "Response to the Investigation Order" on December 24, 2021, and provided the "Application Form for Production Permit of Major Crop Seeds," which indicated that the applicant was Gansu Dunhuang Seed Co., Ltd., the production location was Linze County, Zhangye City, the crop type was corn, and the variety names were "Qiangshuo 68," "Jinnai 99," "Haoyu 318," "Haoyu 8," and "Qiaoyu 1." The application date was May 9, 2008, and the issuance date was June 24, 2008, with the permit number (Gan) Nong Zhong Sheng Xu Zi (2006) No. 0026. Zhitai Company also submitted a "Statement on the Process of Investigation by Entrusted Investigation Order," an audio recording, and a written transcript, showing that the Gansu Provincial Seed Station orally responded that only application forms existed for applications before 2015, and no other archival materials were retained, as they had been destroyed. Upon verification by the court of first instance, the above oral response was found to be true.

With respect to the evidence collected by the court of first instance, Zhitai Company acknowledged its authenticity, legality, and relevance but argued that, according to Article 7, Item 8 of the "Measures for the Administration of Crop Seed Production and Operation Permits," if a variety is an authorized variety, the applicant for a seed production permit must also provide to the reviewing authority a written certificate of consent from the variety rights holder or a variety transfer contract. Authorized varieties include both varieties granted new plant variety rights and approved varieties. Since "Qiangshuo 68" had already passed variety approval before applying for plant variety rights, it indicated that the variety had been authorized by the administrative authority and thus fell under authorized varieties. Therefore, to obtain a production and operation permit for "Qiangshuo 68," a written certificate of consent from the variety rights holder should have been provided. The Gansu Provincial Seed Station only provided the "Application Form for Production Permit of Major Crop Seeds," and other evidentiary materials had clearly been destroyed. The Plant Variety Protection Review Committee acknowledged the authenticity, legality, and relevance but argued that authorized varieties do not include approved varieties; they refer only to varieties granted new plant variety rights, and this evidence could not support Zhitai Company's opinion. Yi Tailong acknowledged the authenticity, legality, and relevance but argued that this evidence could not support Zhitai Company's opinion, as authorized varieties specifically refer to varieties that have obtained new plant variety rights, and Zhitai Company's understanding was mistaken.

In the first instance proceedings, Zhitai Company specified that its basis for claiming that "Qiangshuo 68" lacked novelty was that the propagating material of "Qiangshuo 68" had been sold in China with the breeder's permission for more than one year before the application date. Specifically, it fell under the circumstance of "sale by the breeder himself" as provided in Article 15, Paragraph 2, Item 1 of the Implementing Rules of the Regulations. The specific sales acts included those provided in Article 15, Paragraph 1, Items 1, 2, and 4 of the Implementing Rules. Zhitai Company stated that Evidence 2 submitted in the invalidation proceedings, namely the "Certificate Letter" issued by Zhangye Dunhuang Company to the Shenyang Intermediate People's Court of Liaoning Province on October 20, 2015, recorded that Zhangye Dunhuang Company delivered "Qiangshuo 68" corn seeds to Yi Tailong at a price of RMB 6.3 per kilogram. Evidence 4 submitted by Zhitai Company in the first instance litigation, namely Judgment No. 240, used the RMB 6.3 from the "Certificate Letter" as the unit cost, which meant that the content recorded in the "Certificate Letter" involved a sales act. Therefore, the above two pieces of evidence could prove that the propagating material of "Qiangshuo 68" had been sold in China for more than one year before the application date. Additionally, the "Application Form for Production Permit of Major Crop Seeds" obtained by the court of first instance upon Zhitai Company's application showed that Gansu Dunhuang Company had applied for a seed production permit including "Qiangshuo 68" on May 9, 2008. This application form indicated that Yi Tailong and Gansu Dunhuang Company had carried out production activities, and the entity from which the evidence was obtained admitted that other materials had been destroyed. According to Article 7, Item 8 of the "Measures for the Administration of Crop Seed Production and Operation Permits," there should also be other materials such as production agreements, which should be included in the destroyed materials.

The court of first instance held:

(I) Applicable Law

The application date of the variety in question was December 9, 2009. This case should be adjudicated in accordance with the "Seed Law of the People's Republic of China" (hereinafter referred to as the Seed Law) as amended in 2004, the "Regulations on the Protection of New Plant Varieties" issued in 1997, and the "Implementing Rules of the Regulations" as revised in 2007.

(II) Whether "Qiangshuo 68" Possesses Novelty

1. Relevant provisions on novelty in the Seed Law and the Regulations on the Protection of New Plant Varieties and their interpretation.

Novelty is one of the necessary conditions for a plant variety to obtain new plant variety rights. Article 12 of the Seed Law as amended in 2004 provides: "The State implements a system for the protection of new plant varieties. Plant varieties that have been artificially cultivated or developed from discovered wild plants and possess novelty, distinctness, uniformity, and stability shall be granted new plant variety rights."

Article 14 of the "Regulations on the Protection of New Plant Varieties" issued in 1997 defines novelty: "A new plant variety for which variety rights are to be granted shall possess novelty. Novelty means that, before the application date, the propagating material of the new plant variety for which variety rights are applied has not been sold, or, with the permission of the breeder, the sale of the propagating material of the variety within China has not exceeded one year; the sale of propagating material of vines, forest trees, fruit trees, and ornamental trees outside China has not exceeded six years, and the sale of propagating material of other plant varieties outside China has not exceeded four years."

Article 15 of the Implementing Rules of the Regulations provides: "Any of the following circumstances constitutes a sale as referred to in Article 14 of the Regulations: (1) transferring the propagating material of the applied variety to another person by way of purchase and sale; (2) transferring the propagating material of the applied variety to another person by way of barter; (3) transferring the propagating material of the applied variety to another person by way of equity contribution; (4) entering into a production agreement using the propagating material of the applied variety; (5) other forms of sale. Any of the following circumstances is deemed a sale permitted by the breeder as referred to in Article 14 of the Regulations: (1) sale by the breeder himself; (2) sale by an internal institution of the breeder; (3) sale by a wholly-owned or equity-participating enterprise of the breeder; (4) other circumstances as prescribed by the Ministry of Agriculture."

From the above provisions, first, the novelty of a new plant variety emphasizes the word "new," and the core of the novelty determination lies in the sale of the propagating material of the applied variety, i.e., whether the propagating material of the applied variety was sold before the application date, which essentially means whether the propagating material of the applied variety has entered the public domain and become accessible to the public. Second, according to Article 14 of the Regulations on the Protection of New Plant Varieties, a variety that has not been sold before the application date is clearly novel. At the same time, to maximize the protection of the applicant's rights, a grace period is provided for sales permitted by the breeder, granting the breeder certain preferential treatment. Third, the grace period differs depending on whether the variety is sold within China or outside China and on the biological characteristics of the variety. Furthermore, Article 15, Paragraphs 1 and 2 of the Implementing Rules specify what constitutes a sales act and what circumstances are deemed as breeder-permitted sales.

2. Whether Zhitai Company's grounds for claiming that "Qiangshuo 68" lacks novelty are valid.

Zhitai Company argued that "Qiangshuo 68" lacks novelty because the propagating material of "Qiangshuo 68" had been sold in China with the breeder's permission for more than one year before the application date. Specifically, it fell under the circumstance of "sale by the breeder himself" as provided in Article 15, Paragraph 2, Item 1 of the Implementing Rules, and the specific sales acts included those provided in Article 15, Paragraph 1, Items 1, 2, and 4 of the Implementing Rules. The relevant evidence was Evidence 2 submitted in the invalidation proceedings, namely the "Certificate Letter" issued by Zhangye Dunhuang Company to the Shenyang Intermediate People's Court of Liaoning Province on October 20, 2015. In this regard, the court of first instance held that the "Certificate Letter" issued by Zhangye Dunhuang Company only showed that Zhangye Dunhuang Company had been cultivating "Qiangshuo 68" corn seeds for Yi Tailong since 2008 and delivered "Qiangshuo 68" corn seeds to Yi Tailong at a price of RMB 6.3 per kilogram. This could only reflect that Yi Tailong repurchased the "Qiangshuo 68" corn seeds entrusted to others for cultivation. Judgment No. 240, for the purpose of calculating compensation, referred to the price at which Yi Tailong repurchased the "Qiangshuo 68" corn seeds entrusted to others as the unit cost, but this did not mean that Judgment No. 240 recognized that the content recorded in the "Certificate Letter" involved Yi Tailong's sales act concerning the propagating material of "Qiangshuo 68." The above "Certificate Letter" could not prove that before the application date of "Qiangshuo 68," Yi Tailong transferred the propagating material of "Qiangshuo 68" to others by purchase and sale or barter, or entered into a production agreement using the propagating material of "Qiangshuo 68." That is, the "Certificate Letter" could not prove that before the application date of "Qiangshuo 68," Yi Tailong had already sold the propagating material of "Qiangshuo 68" within China.

Zhitai Company further argued that the "Application Form for Production Permit of Major Crop Seeds" obtained by the court of first instance upon Zhitai Company's application showed that Gansu Dunhuang Company had applied for a seed production permit including "Qiangshuo 68" on May 9, 2008. This application form indicated that Yi Tailong and Gansu Dunhuang Company had carried out production activities. And the entity from which the evidence was obtained admitted that other materials had been destroyed. According to Article 7, Item 8 of the "Measures for the Administration of Crop Seed Production and Operation Permits," there should also be other materials such as production agreements, which should be included in the destroyed materials. In this regard, the court of first instance held that the "Application Form for Production Permit of Major Crop Seeds" could only prove that Gansu Dunhuang Company obtained a seed production permit for "Qiangshuo 68" on June 24, 2008, and was qualified to produce "Qiangshuo 68" corn seeds, but could not prove that Yi Tailong or Gansu Dunhuang Company sold the propagating material of "Qiangshuo 68" to others. According to Article 7, Item 8 of the "Measures for the Administration of Crop Seed Production and Operation Permits," if a variety is an authorized variety, the applicant for a seed production permit must also provide to the reviewing authority a written certificate of consent from the variety rights holder or a variety transfer contract. The understanding of "authorized variety" in this provision should be consistent with the meaning of "variety rights holder" in the same article. The "variety rights holder" is the entity granted new plant variety rights by the competent agricultural and forestry authorities of the State Council. In this case, when Gansu Dunhuang Company applied for the seed production permit for "Qiangshuo 68," Yi Tailong had not yet applied for new plant variety rights for "Qiangshuo 68," and at that time, "Qiangshuo 68" was not yet an authorized variety. Therefore, Zhitai Company's inference that the destroyed materials contained production agreements and other materials that could prove that the propagating material of "Qiangshuo 68" had been sold before the application date could not be established, and the court of first instance did not support it.

In summary, based on the evidence on record, Zhitai Company's claim that "Qiangshuo 68" lacked novelty lacked factual basis. The challenged decision's finding that the variety in question met the novelty requirement was correct, and the court of first instance supported it.

Pursuant to Article 69 of the "Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China," the court of first instance rendered the following judgment: The lawsuit filed by Dalian Zhitai Seed Industry Co., Ltd. was dismissed. The case acceptance fee of RMB 100 was borne by Dalian Zhitai Seed Industry Co., Ltd.

Zhitai Company, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to this Court, requesting: 1. Reversal of the first-instance judgment; 2. Reversal of the challenged decision and an order for the Plant Variety Protection Review Committee to make a new decision; 3. The Plant Variety Protection Review Committee to bear the litigation costs of this case. The facts and reasons were as follows: (I) The "Certificate Letter" issued by Zhangye Dunhuang Company to the Shenyang Intermediate People's Court of Liaoning Province on October 20, 2015, proved that it had been cultivating "Qiangshuo 68" corn seeds for Yi Tailong since 2008, and the corn planting time was spring, indicating that Yi Tailong had already delivered "Qiangshuo 68" seeds to Zhangye Dunhuang Company in the spring of 2008. The content of this "Certificate Letter" was essentially the content of a production agreement. According to the requirement that a production agreement must be provided when applying for a seed production permit, and the content of the above "Certificate Letter," Gansu Dunhuang Company added the corn variety "Qiangshuo 68" to its seed production permit on June 24, 2008. It could be concluded that Yi Tailong had delivered the propagating material of "Qiangshuo 68" to Gansu Dunhuang Company before June 24, 2008, for the production of "Qiangshuo 68" corn seeds. This act exceeded one year before the application date for new plant variety rights. The "Statement on the Production of 'Qiangshuo 68' Corn Hybrid Seeds" issued by Zhangye Dunhuang Company on February 21, 2019, intended to prove that the trial production in 2008 failed, which contradicted the "Certificate Letter." Moreover, Zhangye Dunhuang Company, Gansu Dunhuang Company, and Yi Tailong had an interest relationship. Even if "trial production in 2008" existed, trial production was also a form of production. The first-instance judgment's finding that the evidence on record could not prove that Yi Tailong had sold the propagating material of "Qiangshuo 68" within China before the application date for new plant variety rights was erroneous. (II) The first-instance judgment applied the law incorrectly. The Liaoning Provincial Crop Variety Approval Committee had already approved "Qiangshuo 68" on February 21, 2008. Without a production agreement, it would have been impossible to obtain the seed production permit. Combined with the content of the "Certificate Letter," there must have been a production agreement signed between Gansu Dunhuang Company and Yi Tailong before the application for the seed production permit. Article 7, Item 8 of the "Measures for the Administration of Crop Seed Production and Operation Permits" provides that the production of "authorized varieties" refers to varieties authorized for production between two entities, i.e., the authorized variety, not specifically the "authorized" "new plant variety." Since the novelty determination is based on the time of delivery and signing of production agreements for the variety's propagating material, the propagating material of "Qiangshuo 68" had been sold in China with Yi Tailong's permission for more than one year; therefore, "Qiangshuo 68" lacked novelty.

The Plant Variety Protection Review Committee argued in defense: (I) The core of the novelty determination lies in the sale of the propagating material of the applied variety, i.e., whether the propagating material of the applied variety was sold before the application date, which essentially means whether the propagating material of the applied variety has entered the public domain and become accessible to the public. The determination of a sales act should avoid confusion with use acts. It is necessary not only to examine whether the ownership of the variety has been transferred but also whether there is a genuine intention to sell. The "Certificate Letter" issued by Zhangye Dunhuang Company only showed that it had been producing seeds of "Qiangshuo 68" for Yi Tailong since 2008 and delivered the variety to Yi Tailong at a price of RMB 6.3 per kilogram. This could only reflect that Yi Tailong repurchased the variety entrusted to others for cultivation. The above act was essentially a use act of the variety in question, not a sales act. Yi Tailong did not have the intention to commercially sell the variety in question. Zhitai Company's claim that Yi Tailong had engaged in sales acts of the variety in question and that the variety lacked novelty lacked factual and legal basis. (II) Zhitai Company misunderstood the term "authorized variety" in Article 7, Item 8 of the "Measures for the Administration of Crop Seed Production and Operation Permits." The authorized variety should be consistent with the variety rights holder. When Gansu Dunhuang Company applied for the major crop seed production permit, "Qiangshuo 68" was not yet an authorized variety. Yi Tailong did not engage in acts of selling the variety in question through production agreements or have the intention to commercially sell the variety in question. Zhitai Company's claim could not be established. In summary, the challenged decision and the first-instance judgment had clear facts and correct application of law, requesting the appeal to be dismissed and the original judgment to be affirmed.

Yi Tailong argued: The appeal should be dismissed and the original judgment affirmed.

During the second instance of this case, none of the parties submitted new evidence, and all did not object to the first-instance judgment's determinations on the authenticity, legality, and relevance of the evidence involved.

Separate findings in the second instance: The entity that issued the "Certificate Letter" to the Shenyang Intermediate People's Court of Liaoning Province on October 20, 2015, was Zhangye Dunhuang Company; the "Reply Letter on the Licensing Qualifications of Gansu Dunhuang Seed Co., Ltd. for the 'Qiangshuo 68' Variety" issued by the Gansu Provincial Seed Administration on March 13, 2018, to the Dalian Pulandian Agricultural Administrative Law Enforcement Team, and the "Letter on the Seed Production Permit Status of 'Qiangshuo 68'" issued by the Gansu Provincial Seed Station on July 20, 2020, involved the entity Gansu Dunhuang Company. During the second-instance trial of this case, all parties acknowledged that Zhangye Dunhuang Company and Gansu Dunhuang Company were affiliated companies. The first-instance judgment abbreviated both entities as Dunhuang Company without distinction. This Court corrects this.

The other facts found by the first-instance court are true and are confirmed by this Court.

This Court holds: The application date for the new plant variety rights of "Qiangshuo 68" in question was December 9, 2009. This case should be governed by the "Regulations on the Protection of New Plant Varieties" issued in 1997 and the "Implementing Rules of the Regulations" as revised in 2007.

A variety granted new plant variety rights must possess novelty. According to Articles 21, 27, and 28 of the Regulations on the Protection of New Plant Varieties and Article 21, Item 4 of the Implementing Rules, an applicant for new plant variety protection shall, in the description submitted, provide an explanation of the sales status of the variety. The examining authority shall conduct a preliminary examination of whether the variety right application meets the novelty requirement. For a variety right application that fails the preliminary examination, the examining authority shall notify the applicant to state its views or make corrections within three months; if no response or correction is made within the time limit, or if the correction still fails, the application shall be rejected. Article 37 of the Regulations on the Protection of New Plant Varieties provides: "From the date the examining authority announces the grant of variety rights, the Plant Variety Protection Review Committee may, ex officio or upon written request from any entity or individual, declare the variety rights invalid if they do not comply with Articles 14, 15, 16, and 17 of these Regulations." For an invalidation request filed against an already granted new plant variety, the examining authority generally only reviews the request based on the facts and reasons asserted. If the invalidation requester claims that the variety lacks novelty, it must submit evidence to prove it. This case is an administrative lawsuit filed by Zhitai Company against the challenged decision of the Plant Variety Protection Review Committee on the novelty of "Qiangshuo 68." According to Article 6 of the "Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China," the people's court, when hearing an administrative case, shall review the legality of the administrative act. Regarding whether "Qiangshuo 68" possesses novelty, the review should focus on whether the facts and reasons presented by Zhitai Company can prove its claim, and then review the legality of the administrative act.

The focus of the dispute in this case is whether the first-instance judgment and the appealed decision correctly determined that the variety "Qiangshuo 68" possessed novelty. The appellant, Zhitai Company, appealed on the ground that "Qiangshuo 68" lacks novelty, arguing that the time when Yi Tailong entered into the entrusted production agreement with Gansu Dunhuang Company for the variety in question exceeded one year prior to the filing date of the new plant variety application, which falls under the circumstance of "sale by the breeder himself" as provided in Article 15, paragraph 2, item 1 of the Implementing Rules of the Regulations; and that on June 24, 2008, Gansu Dunhuang Company added the variety "Qiangshuo 68" to its original seed production license by amendment; and that on October 20, 2015, Zhangye Dunhuang Company issued a "Certificate Letter" to the Shenyang Intermediate People's Court of Liaoning Province, certifying that it had been cultivating "Qiangshuo 68" for Yi Tailong since 2008, which falls under the circumstance of "entering into a production agreement using the propagating material of the applied variety" as provided in Article 15, paragraph 1, item 4 of the Implementing Rules of the Regulations. In this regard, this Court analyzes as follows:

First, regarding the standard for determining whether the applied variety possesses novelty. In determining whether a variety for which a new plant variety right is applied possesses novelty, the focus shall be on whether the propagating material of that plant variety has been sold by the breeder himself or with the breeder's authorization within the territory of China for more than one year prior to the filing date, or sold outside China for more than six years for vines and woody plants, and more than four years for other plants. Accordingly, the core issue in this case is whether Yi Tailong sold seeds of "Qiangshuo 68" within the territory of China before December 9, 2008, i.e., one year prior to December 9, 2009, the date on which the application for a new plant variety right for "Qiangshuo 68" was filed.

Second, regarding the relevant evidence of Gansu Dunhuang Company's addition of the "Qiangshuo 68" variety by amendment to the seed production license and its probative force. The appellant, Zhitai Company, argued that "Qiangshuo 68" became an authorized variety as early as February 21, 2008, upon being approved by the Liaoning Provincial Variety Approval Committee; that to add this variety by amendment to the seed production license, Gansu Dunhuang Company would have needed authorization from the breeder, Yi Tailong; and that therefore, there must have been a production agreement signed between Yi Tailong and Gansu Dunhuang Company and a delivery of "Qiangshuo 68" seeds. In this regard, this Court holds that an approved variety is one that has obtained an approval certificate through administrative procedures; it is different from obtaining a new plant variety right, which is a civil right. Obtaining variety approval does not mean that the applicant acquires an exclusive civil right. Article 7, item 8 of the Measures for the Administration of Crop Seed Production and Operation Licenses provides that "if the variety is an authorized variety, an application for a seed production license shall also submit to the reviewing authority a written certificate of consent from the variety rights holder or a variety transfer contract." The term "authorized variety" in that provision shall refer to a variety for which a new plant variety right has been obtained. The authorization date for the "Qiangshuo 68" variety was March 1, 2014. When Gansu Dunhuang Company added "Qiangshuo 68" by amendment to its original seed production license on June 24, 2008, "Qiangshuo 68" was not yet an authorized variety, and thus it clearly does not fall under the circumstance described in the aforementioned Measures for the Administration of Crop Seed Production and Operation Licenses, i.e., requiring submission of a written certificate of consent from the variety rights holder when applying for a seed production license. Zhitai Company's mere assertion that, because Gansu Dunhuang Company added "Qiangshuo 68" by amendment to its original seed production license, Yi Tailong must have signed a production agreement with Gansu Dunhuang Company, lacks supporting effective evidence and is insufficient to prove the fact that Yi Tailong sold the propagating material of "Qiangshuo 68".

Third, regarding the "Certificate Letter" issued by Zhangye Dunhuang Company and its probative force. The appellant, Zhitai Company, argued that the "Certificate Letter" states that Zhangye Dunhuang Company had been producing "Qiangshuo 68" corn seeds since 2008; that the company accepted the entrustment of Yi Tailong and, starting in 2008, cultivated "Qiangshuo 68" corn seeds for Yi Tailong; that this indicates Yi Tailong delivered the propagating material of "Qiangshuo 68" to Zhangye Dunhuang Company in 2008; and that even if it were merely trial seed production, it still constitutes an act of production, and the content of the "Certificate Letter" is essentially the content of a production agreement. In this regard, this Court holds that whether a sale exists is an important fact for determining whether the applied variety possesses novelty. According to Article 14 of the Regulations on the Protection of New Plant Varieties, a sale that causes the variety applied for a new plant variety right to lose novelty refers to an act by which the actor, for the purpose of transaction, delivers the variety's propagating material to another person for disposition, thereby relinquishing the actor's own right to dispose of that propagating material. When a breeder delivers the propagating material of the applied variety for the purpose of entrusting another person to produce seeds, and agrees that the produced variety's propagating material shall be returned to the breeder, the breeder effectively retains the right to dispose of that variety's propagating material. Unless otherwise provided by law, this does not cause the applied variety to lose novelty. In this case, according to the content recorded in the "Certificate Letter", the "Qiangshuo 68" seeds produced by Zhangye Dunhuang Company were to be delivered to Yi Tailong; Yi Tailong entrusted that company to produce seeds and was obligated to pay the seed production fee to repurchase the "Qiangshuo 68" seeds produced by Zhangye Dunhuang Company; the intention of both parties regarding the entrustment of seed production and repurchase was clear. Zhitai Company did not present any contrary evidence to overturn the fact of such entrustment for seed production and repurchase. Although Zhangye Dunhuang Company held and used the propagating material of "Qiangshuo 68" for a certain period, it had no right to dispose of the propagating material of "Qiangshuo 68" or to take any other action inconsistent with the entrusted production contract. Yi Tailong, as the entrusting party, did not relinquish the right to dispose of the applied variety's propagating material. Therefore, Yi Tailong's act of entrusting Zhangye Dunhuang Company to produce "Qiangshuo 68" and repurchasing it does not constitute a sale of the propagating material of "Qiangshuo 68".

The existing evidence submitted by Zhitai Company in this case is insufficient to prove that "Qiangshuo 68" has lost novelty. The appealed decision and the first-instance judgment did not err in this determination, and this Court upholds them. Zhitai Company's appeal claim that "Qiangshuo 68" lacks novelty cannot be sustained, and this Court does not support it.

In summary, the appeal request of Zhitai Company cannot be sustained and shall be dismissed. The first-instance judgment, which found the facts clearly and applied the law correctly, shall be affirmed. Pursuant to Article 89, paragraph 1, item 1 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

The appeal is dismissed and the original judgment is affirmed.

The second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 100 shall be borne by Dalian Zhitai Seed Industry Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final.
